newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister insists Papon trial on time.
newsitem.headline: French minister insists Papon trial on time.

text.p: French Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou says the trial of former cabinet minister Maurice Papon for alleged wartime crimes against humanity must start as scheduled on October 6 despite the need for courtroom renovation.

"I'm being told that the hearing has to be delayed in order to install a new courtroom. I reply that the trial must be held at the scheduled date," Guigou told the daily Le Figaro in an interview to be published on Tuesday.

Justice officials have said the long-awaited trial in the southwest city of Bordeaux could be delayed for several months because plans to build a large courtroom to accommodate demand for press and public seating were more costly than expected.
Guigou said she was looking for a technical solution to avoid delaying the trial, expected to last two to three months.
The threat of further delays in the trial of the 86-year-old former official has angered relatives of his alleged wartime victims who have fought to bring him to justice since 1981.
Papon is accused of ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews to Nazi death camps in 1942-44 when he served as wartime secretary-general of the Bordeaux region under the Vichy government.
He has denied guilt and insisted he used his position to help the Resistance fighting France's Nazi conquerors.

Papon enjoyed an illustrious post-war career until the discovery of dusty wartime files documenting his arrests and deportation orders. He served as Paris police chief in 1958-67 and budget minister in the 1970s, and was named commander of the Legion of Honour, France's highest honour.
